newsitem.title: USA: FAA grants GE-powered Boeing 777 ETOPS approval.
newsitem.headline: FAA grants GE-powered Boeing 777 ETOPS approval.

text.p: Boeing Co Thursday said the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration has granted extended-range twin-engine operations, or ETOPS, approval to Boeing 777 airliners powered by General Electric Co's GE90 engines.

Boeing said the FAA approval acknowledges that the engine/aircraft design is reliable for ETOPS qualification. This allows twin-engine aircraft to fly long-distance routes, many over water, up to 180 minutes flying time from primary and alternate airports.

As of Sept. 16, the aircraft maker said 37 Boeing 777s have been delivered to eight customers worldwide and have experienced a cumulative schedule reliability exceeding 98 percent. Orders for the twin-engine airplane now total 281 from 22 customers.
